about: Gyropup's pronunciation key: what a written word or name is turned into before it is spoken. One file for every voice: designer/character/pronounce.js (the browser and the live Piper sidecar requests), tools/pronunciation.py (tools/tts_server.py and the clip renderer tools/render-voice.py). Matching is case-insensitive and whole-word; possessives and plurals ('s, s', s) keep their ending; URLs, e-mail addresses and domain names are never changed. 'say' is a plain respelling sent to every engine. Stress is set by how it is split: a space makes separate words, each stressed ('gyro pup'); a hyphen joins syllables into one word stressed on its first part ('sigh-an'). Never use capitals for stress: espeak spells an all-caps word letter by letter. See designer/character/README.md.

entries.why: The owner: two words, so it is said 'gyro pup'. espeak runs it together as one word, JYE-ruh-pup (dʒˈaɪɹəpˌʌp); 'gyro pup' gives dʒˈaɪɹoʊ pˈʌp.
Said TRIT-ee-um. espeak says TRY-tee-um (tɹˈaɪɾiəm); 'Trittium' gives tɹˈɪɾiəm.
Stress on the first syllable, SIGH-an. espeak stresses the second (saɪˈæn); the hyphen joins the syllables and stresses the first (sˈaɪæn).
espeak says 'aw-uh' (ˈɔːwə) for the double w; 'aw' is ˈɔː.
espeak spells it out, 'zee zee zee'. No plain spelling makes espeak buzz, so the sleepy line says 'snore' (the owner may prefer another word).
